title: Lonely runner conjecture: dense windows and the covering framework, an obstruction catalogue, a perturbation bound, a reduction, and eight runners, with leave-one-out values of tight Goddyn-Wong vectors
description: Seven manuscripts on the lonely runner conjecture (dense velocity windows, obstructions to certificate-based proofs, perturbations of the tight instance, a reduction to a single crux, a covering framework, eight runners, and leave-one-out values of tight Goddyn-Wong vectors), the Lean 4 sources they cite, and the programs and certificates that regenerate their finite computations. Version 1.4.0 contains the content of versions 1.1.0, 1.1.1, 1.2.0, 1.3.0 and 1.3.1 (versions 1.1.1 and 1.3.1 were patch releases with prior-art text corrections only): (1) the dense-window inequality ML >= 1/(m+1) for m distinct speeds in [1,2m] is proved by a short argument when 2m+1 is prime (Theorem D) and is Lean-verified for every m with 2 <= m <= 126, the composite 2m+1 by finite certificates (fractional blocking, cover capacity), including m = 94 by a tree of three pinned cover-capacity certificates (Lean declaration dense_floor_m94; builds of 2026-10 and 2026-11 in the development repository (prime case: one archived print of 2026-10-01), carried over to this archive, not rebuilt); (2) the eight-runner manuscript records the Lean theorem eight_runners_unconditional_real, which depends only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound, compiled with raw lean outside the lake build and re-observed on 2026-11-01, a formalization of a theorem of Rosenfeld; (3) added in version 1.2.0: a Markdown note with a hand proof, and a Lean proof (theorem TPp_four, standard axioms only, builds of 2026-11-12 in the development repository, carried over, not rebuilt), that for any four distinct positive integer speeds v_i and any integers s_i there is a real t with dist(v_i t + s_i/5, Z) >= 1/5 for every i. This is a special case (phases restricted to the grid (1/5)Z, not arbitrary real phases) of the shifted lonely runner conjecture for four moving runners, already proved with computer assistance by Alcantara, Criado and Santos (arXiv:2506.13379; journal status not checked); our contribution is a hand proof not using their enumeration of 2,133,561 velocity vectors, and its Lean version, which relies on the previously formalized unshifted theorem for four speeds (five_runners). Distinctness of the speeds is necessary (v = (1,1,1,5), s = (0,1,3,0) has no solution). (4) new in version 1.3.0: a second Markdown note with a computation-free proof following the Lean proof, and a Lean proof (theorems R5, R5_core, R5_tp, R5_gcd, standard axioms only, builds of 2026-11-12 in the development repository, carried over, not rebuilt, not using five_runners), that for four distinct positive integer speeds v_i with gcd 1, at least one divisible by 5, and arbitrary real phases phi_i, there is a real t with dist(v_i t + phi_i, Z) >= 1/5 for every i. This is a special case of the shifted lonely runner conjecture for four moving runners, proved with computer assistance by Alcantara, Criado and Santos (arXiv:2506.13379, Corollary 1.4; version 1 read locally; journal status not checked); it is not a new theorem. Prior art, corrected in version 1.3.1: as we read Malikiosis, Santos and Schymura (arXiv:2411.06903, version 2; Corollary 1.11, Proposition 2.9 and Proposition 6.5 with n = 4), they treat the shifted conjecture for four moving runners, without a computer search of their own, when the speeds divided by their gcd have sum at least 196 and when two of them have a common divisor that is odd and at least 5 or even and at least 10, so the parts of the result with at least two speeds divisible by 5, or with speed sum at least 196, are not new even as computation-free statements; what we did not find in the sources read is a computation-free proof of the case of exactly one speed divisible by 5 with speed sum at most 195, a finite family of speed vectors, each with all real phases (unrefereed; this does not show that none exists; the proofs of that paper were not re-verified; the published version of Alcantara-Criado-Santos, Beck-Hosten-Schymura, Rifford, the journal version of Malikiosis-Santos-Schymura, the remainder of Barajas-Serra and further papers were not read, as of version 1.3.1; the reading since then is listed under (5)). Speed vectors with no multiple of 5 after removing common factors are not covered; these include the vectors (1,2,3,4), (1,3,4,6), (1,3,4,7) that are tight in the paper of Alcantara, Criado and Santos. The constant 1/5 is not claimed sharp for this class (the smallest value found in computer searches is 5/24 at the speeds (2,3,5,7), computed evidence only). Distinctness of the speeds is necessary (v = (1,1,1,5), phases (0,1/5,3/5,0) has no solution). (5) new in version 1.4.0: a third Markdown note, with written proofs that follow Lean proofs (theorems P3, Q4, QGen, T, G24, with the supporting window_lemma and lemmaC_real; standard axioms only, builds of 2026-11-12 in the development repository, carried over, not rebuilt), of five classes of speed vectors for which four pairwise distinct positive integer speeds v_i and arbitrary real phases phi_i admit a real t with dist(v_i t + phi_i, Z) >= 1/5 for every i: (P3) some q >= 2 divides exactly three of the speeds; (Q4) 4 divides two speeds, the other two are odd, and neither speed divisible by 4 equals the sum or the absolute difference of the two odd speeds; (QGen) the same with any q >= 4, the other two speeds being coprime to q and congruent up to sign modulo q; (T) some q >= 6 divides two speeds and the other two are coprime to q; (G24) two speeds are odd, one is 2 mod 4, one is 0 mod 4 and is not the sum or the absolute difference of the two odd speeds. None is a new theorem: all are special cases of the shifted lonely runner conjecture for four moving runners (five runners), proved with computer assistance by Alcantara, Criado and Santos (arXiv:2506.13379, version 1, Corollary 1.4 there; the numbering and the content of the published version were not checked). As we read Malikiosis, Santos and Schymura (arXiv:2411.06903, version 2; the numbers of its propositions and corollaries are those of version 2), P3 is their Proposition 2.9 at four runners on vectors of gcd 1, the vectors of T with a witness q >= 7, q != 8 lie inside their Proposition 6.5, and QGen with q >= 5 adds nothing beyond earlier results; the residue-shift and pigeonhole mechanism is classical for zero phases (Barajas-Serra; Bohman-Holzman-Kleitman, a related device; Rosenfeld; Allikvere); we did not find, in the texts read, a computation-free proof for arbitrary real phases of the classes with a divisible pair of gcd 4, 6 or 8 or of G24, nor a real-phase form of the window lemma (unrefereed; this does not show that none exists; for G24, the same parity pattern, 2-adic valuations 0, 0, 1 and at least 2, occurs at zero phases in a reduction stated, without its argument, in the four-page conference abstract of Barajas-Serra on distance graphs, and the full paper was not obtained; read end to end: Cslovjecsek et al., Barajas-Serra, Malikiosis-Santos-Schymura, Bohman-Holzman-Kleitman, Beck-Hosten-Schymura, Henze-Malikiosis; read in part: Rifford, 1,236 of 3,437 text lines; not obtained: the published version of Alcantara-Criado-Santos, the journal versions of Malikiosis-Santos-Schymura, the full Barajas-Serra paper on distance graphs, Renault, Bienia et al., Cusick-Pomerance). Census (computed; program and outputs archived): of the 2,133,561 primitive speed vectors with speed sum at most 195, 1,867,559 lie in a class with a Lean proof in this archive, 644,918 in such a class and in neither of the two classes of Malikiosis-Santos-Schymura as we read them, and 266,002 in no class (they include (1,2,3,4), (1,3,4,6), (1,3,4,7)); vectors with speed sum at least 196 are not treated in this archive, which therefore does not contain a proof of the shifted theorem for four moving runners. The class and non-resonance hypotheses are limits of the method and are not shown to be necessary; distinct speeds are necessary; the constant 1/5 is not claimed sharp for any of the five classes; two further lemmas of the same method are neither formalised nor claimed. No whole-library lake build was run. Statements carry the labels given in each manuscript: VERIFIED means formalized in Lean 4 in the development repository, carried over to this archive without a rebuild; PROVED means a written proof not formalized; COMPUTED means an exact finite computation; HEURISTIC means computation only; CONJECTURE means no proof. Statement of significance: Tao's 2017 blog post describes the bound 1/(m+1) for speeds in [1,1.2m] (the proof is in the accompanying preprint arXiv:1701.02048) and names [1,2m] as a sub-problem; to our knowledge no paper proves it for all sets of m distinct speeds in [1,2m], either in general or for an infinite family of m (a negative search of 2026-11-09; the papers of Bohman and Peng, Pomerance and Pandey were read afterwards, on 2026-11-09, and none states the window; the published Mathematika text of Bohman and Peng was not read). The dense-window result is a special case of the conjecture, single-author and unrefereed. WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED: a proof of the lonely runner conjecture; the dense-window statement for any m >= 127 with 2m+1 composite, or for all m; that the manuscripts are refereed; that the Lean tree was rebuilt for this release (no Lean build and no whole-lake build was run; the sources are provided as is and the default target does not build as archived); that the eight-runner theorem without extra axioms was rebuilt (its 27 kernel proofs were kept as object files outside this archive and not rebuilt); that the exhaustive hitting-set computation for m = 94, reported as corroboration, is archived or independently reproduced; that the computations have been independently reproduced; that the four-runner result of version 1.2.0 is a new theorem, holds for arbitrary real phases, or covers more than four moving runners; that the proof of five_runners was re-derived for this release; that the result of version 1.3.0 is a new theorem, covers speed vectors without a multiple of 5, covers repeated speeds or more than four moving runners, or has a sharp constant for its class; that its computation-free proof is new for speed vectors with at least two speeds divisible by 5 or with speed sum (after dividing by the gcd) at least 196; that the prose proof of version 1.3.0 has had an independent read; that the result of version 1.4.0 includes a new theorem, covers any of the 266,002 vectors of the census that lie in no class or any vector with speed sum at least 196, has a sharp constant, or has hypotheses shown to be necessary; that the written proofs of version 1.4.0 are new for P3, for T with a witness q >= 7, q != 8, or for QGen with q >= 5; that the prose of version 1.4.0 has had an independent read. Several results are known or partly known (Beck-Everett, Zhang, Giri-Kravitz, Czerwinski, Bedert, Tao, Rosenfeld, Barajas-Serra); attributions are given in the manuscripts. Counts without an archived generator are marked in CLAIMS.tsv. The leave-one-out note has written proofs relative to two quoted results (Goddyn-Wong Theorem 2.3; Dusart bounds on the prime counting function) and exact computations for small cases; it is not formalized in Lean. The results were obtained with the assistance of an AI system (Claude, Anthropic). The questions and research directions came from the author. The written proofs, programs, certificate searches and Lean sources were produced by the AI system; the Lean theorems are checked by the Lean kernel, and written arguments, Lean statements and computations were read or re-run by further sessions of the same system. The author is responsible for all claims.
